plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win, while bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. Since my value is $21, bidding $21 ensures I win whenever profitable (paying less than $21) and never overpay.

This is a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Bidding exactly my value ensures I never overpay (since I'd only pay what others bid, which would be less than my value if I win) and never miss out on profitable wins. Bidding higher risks overpaying if I win at a price above my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $22, I will bid exactly $22 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the optimal (weakly dominant) strategy. If I bid my true value of $13, I win whenever the second-highest bid is below $13, paying that second-highest bid, ensuring non-negative profit. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value.
